headline: LLM pipelines extract toxicology and mutation evidence from literature into knowledge bases
label: Llm Literature Curation Pipelines
summary: Three toxicology tools and ThermoMutDB 2.0 apply LLM-based extraction to turn large literature corpora into structured, queryable evidence resources.
synthesis: The dominant thread is LLM-based extraction of structured evidence from the biomedical literature. Toxicology accounts for three of these preprints. AOP-Smart-Finder combines LLMs and RAG in a human-AI hybrid framework that mines biological events and key event relationships for AOP discovery. AOPTK provides an open-source Python toolkit for retrieving and extracting chemical-effect relationships. A continuous pipeline mines PubMed/PMC full texts into a hepatotoxicity knowledge base of 189,212 findings across 17,002 chemicals, which is then used for downstream model training. ThermoMutDB 2.0 applies the same approach to protein data, using semiautomated LLM-plus-rule curation to add 1763 thermostability mutation entries, each paired with a mutant structural model. The new element is continuous, semiautomated curation at corpus scale, with human review retained in hybrid designs. The Chemical Probes Portal update, by contrast, remains expert-reviewed and manually curated. KinaseMD 2.0 and a network-based natural-product atlas are adjacent resource efforts and are not described as LLM-driven.
